text:
julie_s: FYI — Acme Customer: sudden p99 spike on /v1/embeddings in us-west-2 after yesterday's infra push. They see p95 ~220ms, p99 ~1.8s (was ~320ms/480ms). They sent traces and a couple of logs. :rotating_light:

mike_sre: Thx. Any correlation with driver/firmware/kernel rollouts? Which clusters are affected?

julie_s: They hit us-west-2-rg-3 and -4. Platform release notes show GPU driver 535.86 + NVMe fw 2.1.4 rolled at 03:10 UTC last night. Kernel 6.5.12 rolled in the same window. I'm attaching their sample trace (shortened):

julie_s: ```
HTTP POST /v1/embeddings 200 1850ms
  tokenization: 18ms
  send-kv: 50ms
  infer (gpu): 1580ms
  nvme-io: 120ms (job waiting on io)
  postproc: 60ms
```

ali_perf: That infer time bump + nvme line suggests host storage tail latency bleeding into overall request time. Could be NVMe queue depth or firmware QoS. I'll pull p95/p99 for root cause.

deploybot: Deploy event: driver-upgrade-535.86 -> completed 2026-03-02T03:10:21Z on us-west-2-rg-* (tags: kernel-6.5.12, nvme-fw-2.1.4).

liu_ops: I just checked host-level iostat on a sampled node in rg-3: ```r/s: 230 w/s: 10 await: 35.2 r_await: 34.9 svctm: 1.2 util: 98.5%``` — NVMe queue saturated on some workers. Also seeing lots of small random writes from KV cache flushes.

mike_sre: Do we have a repro? Can we push synthetic load that matches request size and token lengths? If NVMe is the vector we can validate by temporarily routing to a node with previous NVMe fw/driver.

nate_runtime: Quick note: our runtime fallback policy should route to cpu-fallback only if gpu inference fails, so this is not helping latency. We have a warm pool with older driver in the same region (rg-1) that hasn't been upgraded; we can start routing a % of Acme traffic there as mitigation.

tara_cs: Acme is reporting customer impact — engineering asks for permission to move 30% of traffic now. They are ok with partial routing if it fixes tail.

ali_perf: Mitigations plan: 1) route 30% of Acme requests to rg-1 (older driver/fw) 2) throttle KV cache flush frequency on affected nodes 3) increase batch timeout to reduce tiny-batch pressure 4) collect iostat/nvme top counters and perf events for 24h.

liu_ops: I can toggle the KV cache flush param on the affected autoscaling group. Which param? `kvcache.flush_interval_ms` currently 1500. Suggest bump to 6000 for 2 hours.

mike_sre: Do it — set a rolling change behind a feature flag and monitor p99. Also start routing 30% to rg-1; I'll update routing policy.

nate_runtime: Routing rule applied: Acme traffic split 70/30 to rg-3/rg-1 now (deploy id 2026-03-02T11:45Z).

oncall_bot: Pager muted for 15m while mitigation in progress (reason: routing experiment).

julie_s: Customer confirmed p99 dropped to ~620ms within 12 minutes after split. They see no errors. :thumbsup:

ali_perf: Good signal. Still need to triage host NVMe behavior. I want `nvme smart-log` from one of the problematic devices and `fio` pattern runs to measure tail at small random io size seen by kvcache.

liu_ops: Collected smart-log and kernel ring buffer. Notable dmesg entries: `nvme_core: power state change 1->2` and a couple `nvme: timeout: qpair` warnings during the upgrade window. I will schedule a host to repro using fio pattern (4k randrw, 80/20, iodepth 64) and capture latencies.

mike_sre: If we reproduce elevated tail only with driver 535.86 + fw 2.1.4 + kernel 6.5.12, we'll need to coordinate rollback vs vendor fw update. Contacted HW vendor on slack.

nate_runtime: Also flagging that our KV cache writes produce many small writes; we should consider coalescing or buffering to reduce IO amplification. That's medium-term.

tara_cs: Acme asked for ETA on permanent fix. Suggested telling them we're doing mitigation and will follow up within 48h with root cause and permanent plan.

mike_sre: Action items: 
- liu_ops: run fio + collect perf counters (owner)
- ali_perf: run comparative p99 analysis (owner)
- nate_runtime: start proposal for KV flush coalescing (owner)
- julie_s: keep Acme updated (owner)

mike_sre: If fio repro shows 95th-99th tail expanded under driver/fw combo, we'll prepare rollback runbook for driver to previous stable (535.20) and coordinate with SRE for supervised rollback.

liu_ops: Fio started on host-a1: `fio --name=kv-sim --rw=randrw --bs=4k --size=10G --iodepth=64 --numjobs=8` capturing latencies. Will post results in 30m.

ali_perf: Monitoring shows p99 for Acme now stable ~600ms. I'll keep dashboards pinned and alert thresholds lowered for 2x sensitivity while we finish triage.

mike_sre: Thanks team. Once we have fio + nvme logs we'll decide rollback vs vendor fw patch. Keep this channel updated.

julie_s: Noted. I'll file an incident ticket and forward customer's contact.

deploybot: Incident created: INC-2026-1789 (priority P1 -> P2 if stabilized)

liu_ops: Fio results (summary): p50 2.1ms p95 27ms p99 340ms p999 1.2s — clear long tail under load. nvme qdepth backlog spikes aligned with those p999 events.

mike_sre: That's actionable. Vendor support says fw 2.1.4 has a known rare tail case under high random io on certain controllers; they have a 2.1.5 candidate. We'll test 2.1.5 on staging before mass upgrade. For prod, we should roll driver back to 535.20 on rg-3/r-4 while we validate fw 2.1.5.

nate_runtime: I'll draft driver rollback runbook and list safety checks (gradual percentage rollback, warm pools, kill-switch flag).

tara_cs: Customer updated: appreciate the quick mitigation and asked to be informed for the scheduled rollback window.

mike_sre: Closing loop: mitigation already reduced impact. Next updates after fw test and rollback runbook.
